notes: Dev ABox revision whose edited relation carries transitivity. belongs_to_language_group (staged: transitive, asymmetric, inverse includes_language) holds between a language and each group it sits in (branch, family). The edit moves Hungarian from the Finno-Ugric branch (Uralic family) into the Slavic branch of Indo-European; families are disjoint, so the Uralic membership goes with it. Derived: transitivity (Slavic within Balto-Slavic), a role chain through author_wrote_in (a poet who wrote in Hungarian wrote in every group Hungarian belongs to), and a binding through the endonym 'Magyar'. The direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual and binding questions and the chain question offer the four groups Finno-Ugric, Slavic, Germanic and Romance, since belongs_to_language_group is many-valued and transitive and an unqualified 'which group' would also be answered fairly by Uralic, Indo-European or Balto-Slavic. 'Finno-Ugric' is the usual name for Hungarian's group (Wikipedia's finer label is Ugric); no rank such as 'branch' is named. Unrelated near asks Finnish, Hungarian's best-known relative; an edit that drags the family along would answer Slavic there. Related (one question): which of Finnish, Polish, French or Greek Hungarian is most closely related to (Finnish, then Polish once Hungarian is Slavic; composition through the group of Polish, 2 hops, a fact about a different language). The formal file reads 'most closely related' as sharing a language group with Hungarian, with Polish's membership of Slavic a firm background fact.
